title: Swap the hotend on a Bambu Lab A1 mini 3D printer: buckle open, old hotend to its holder, new one seated, locked
instruction: Change the 3D printer's hotend: open the buckle, take the old hotend out and stand it in the empty slot of the holder, then push the new hotend up into the toolhead until it seats and lock the buckle.
context: Bambu Lab's hotend replacement for the A1 series (Bambu Lab wiki, Hotend Replacement for A1 Series; the A1 mini takes the same hotend): with the printer off and cool, the filament cut and the toolhead's front cover and silicone sock off, push the nozzle buckle to unlock it and swing it open, hold the heatsink and pull the hotend out, put the new one in until it sits flush (a magnet aligns it) and close the buckle; if the buckle will not lock, the hotend is not seated. Owners swap hotends to clear clogs, replace worn or damaged nozzles or change size (0.2 mm for fine detail, 0.4 mm standard, hardened steel for abrasive filament). Done by printer owners, makerspace staff and print-farm technicians. Low-cost robot arms are built from such prints: the SO-ARM100 printing guide (for Hugging Face's LeRobot) lists Bambu Lab A/P/X-series printers, and XLeRobot's parts were printed on a Bambu Lab A1. A robot that keeps printers running can make more robot parts with less human help.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Bambu Lab A1 mini 3D printer, powered off and cold, front toward the robot; a loose 5.5 kg block model: base 28 x 24 x 7 cm (x 27.5 to 55.5, y -12 to 12) with an 18 x 18 cm bed (top 7.6 cm up); Z column 6 x 5 x 31 cm at the right rear (x 46.5 to 52.5, y -17 to -12); X arm 3 x 25 x 3 cm behind the toolhead at 25 to 28 cm. Toolhead (front cover and silicone sock off, filament cut): 3.5 x 5.4 x 7.5 cm, x 36.5 to 40, y -2.7 to 2.7, underside 20 cm up; in it a 1.5 x 2.1 cm hotend pocket 1.2 cm deep at x 37.5, y 0, with a 1.4 cm wide, 1.1 cm high window in its front wall, and a sprung catch in its back wall that presses the hotend forward with about 0.4 N (for the A1's magnet). Buckle: a 2.8 cm metal bar on a vertical hinge at x 36.3, y -1.2 (the window's right), 20.2 to 20.5 cm up, with a 1.2 x 1 x 0.7 cm tab at its left end; closed it lies along the window under the hotend's lug; its left end swings out to the front, up to 90 degrees. Two Bambu Hotend - A1 Series hotends, each simplified to a 1.2 x 1.8 x 4.6 cm heatsink with a 0.7 x 1 x 0.4 cm lug on its front just below the top and a 0.7 cm nozzle, 6 cm overall, 22 g: the old one (0.4 mm, dark band) seated in the pocket; the new one (0.2 mm, green tag) standing nozzle-down in the holder's right slot. Holder: printed PLA, 200 g, loose: a 4 x 16 x 8 cm block (x 23 to 27, y -5 to 11) with two 1.1 x 1.8 x 2 cm bosses on top (tops 10 cm up), each with a 0.9 cm square hole: the right slot at y -3.5 (new hotend), the left one at y 9.5 (empty).
scoring: Score = 0.2 x old out + 0.4 x new seated + 0.3 x locked + 0.1 x finished; 0 if the new hotend is dropped. Old out: the old hotend stands in a holder slot (axis within 0.3 cm of the slot's, heatsink on the boss within 0.3 cm, within 8 degrees of upright) and was not dropped on the way. Dropped: a hotend falls 2 cm within 0.5 s with no finger pad within 1.5 cm of its heatsink while not in the pocket or a slot, or its nozzle tip reaches the bed or the table. New seated: the new hotend's top within 0.15 cm of the pocket's top, its axis within 0.25 cm of the seat and within 4 degrees of vertical. Locked: the buckle within 3 degrees of its closed stop while the new hotend is seated (closed, its bar lies 0.15 cm under a seated hotend's lug). The catch holds a hotend only once it is pushed fully home: one let go short of its seat slides out and falls. Finished: seated and locked, no finger pad within 1 cm of the new hotend's heatsink or the buckle's tab, and the hotend and buckle still (under 0.15 cm of motion) for 20 steps (1 s); the run is a success, and ends, once that has held 1 s with the old hotend in a slot. Real trial: the same from photos and video; seated means the buckle locks (Bambu: it will not lock over an unseated hotend), a 0.1 mm feeler does not enter between the heatsink and the heating assembly, and the hotend does not wobble when wiggled by hand after the run (Bambu's check).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the old hotend back in the pocket and close the buckle, stand the new hotend in the holder's right slot, and put the printer and the holder back on their tape marks. Real trials: the printer stays off and cool (below 50 C) with the front cover and silicone sock off and the filament cut; the two hotends may swap roles between trials.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The printer is a loose 5.5 kg block model; its toolhead is part of it (the real carriage slides along X when the printer is off). The hotend is simplified: 6 cm long (the real one 4.73 cm) with a 1.2 x 1.8 cm heatsink, 22 g (estimated). Its magnet and heater are a 1.2 cm deep pocket with a sprung catch (about 0.4 N) that holds it by friction; the buckle is a hinged bar that closes 0.15 cm under a seated hotend's lug (the real one also slides to lock).
